workflows.name: How a chat turn runs
workflows.summary: A message goes to the agent runtime on the server, which saves it, builds the prompt from the user’s saved data, calls the model and runs the tools it asks for, and streams progress back to the page. The turn keeps going if the tab closes.
workflows.trigger: The user presses Send in chat, or another page sends a message such as New goal, Do it or Ask Muse to move this forward

steps.action: Submits a message from the composer or a feature button
steps.label: Sends a message

steps.action: Shows the message, disables the composer and posts it with the response tier and time zone
steps.label: Post the turn

steps.action: Refuses if another turn for this user is still live, then saves the user message and a live reply
steps.label: Save the messages

steps.action: Builds the tools and runs the shortcuts: Library check for résumé steps, a job-research nudge, opening an application link
steps.label: Tools and shortcuts

steps.action: Builds the system prompt from saved memory, ideas, goals and settings, plus the last 18 messages
steps.label: Build the prompt

steps.action: Streams a model turn with the server-held key and a model picked from the tier
steps.label: Ask the model

steps.action: Asks for tools; the runtime runs each one, logs it and feeds the result back
steps.label: Run the tools

steps.action: Streams events to the page and saves the reply every few seconds
steps.label: Stream progress

steps.action: Ends the turn: expires unanswered approvals, marks the reply finished and saves it
steps.label: Finish the turn

errorPaths: No API key: the turn ends with sampling_disabled; the page shows the assistant-unavailable message and disables the composer.
Model errors 401, 403, 429 and 400 map to session_expired, not_granted, rate_limited, prompt_too_large or refused.
A tool that throws, or an unknown tool, goes back to the model as an error result instead of ending the turn.
Stop, from any device, cancels the turn through /api/agent/cancel; no error is shown.
If the page’s stream drops, the turn keeps running; the page polls /api/state until the reply is finished.
If another turn is live, the server answers busy and the page puts the text back in the composer.
The serverless call is capped at 300 seconds, so a very long turn can be cut off.

workflows.name: How sensitive actions get approval
workflows.summary: Before a tool changes or sends something, the agent runtime saves an approval card and waits. The user answers on any device; the change runs only if they approved.
workflows.trigger: The model calls a tool that writes, such as sending an email, adding a calendar event or revising a goal

steps.action: Calls a write tool
steps.label: Calls a write tool

steps.action: Checks whether it needs approval: Gmail always asks; Calendar and Contacts follow the user’s Ask or Allow setting
steps.label: Ask or allow?

steps.action: Adds a pending card to the reply, saves it and creates a wait record
steps.label: Save the card

steps.action: Shows the card; another device shows it too after loading the chat
steps.label: Show the card

steps.action: Allows or declines the action
steps.label: Answer the card

steps.action: Posts the answer; only a pending wait can be answered, so a second answer gets 409
steps.label: Post the answer

steps.action: Wakes the waiting turn, records the answer and an audit entry, and runs the change only if approved
steps.call: the approved write, such as mail send
steps.label: Run if approved

steps.action: Returns the result to the model, or Nothing was changed if declined or unanswered
steps.label: Return the result

errorPaths: A decline returns “The user declined. Nothing was changed.” to the model.
No answer within 4 minutes (AGENT_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_MS), or Stop, expires the card and returns “The user did not answer. Nothing was changed.”

If the turn reaches its time limit (AGENT_TURN_BUDGET_MS, 270s) while the card is open, the turn pauses with the card open; an answer within the card's 4 minutes returns resume, and the browser posts a follow-up turn that re-runs the tool with that answer. A later answer is refused (409).

workflows.name: How a goal step advances
workflows.summary: A goal is planned as steps, and a step only moves forward when a tool did real work in the same turn. The agent runtime enforces this on the server.
workflows.trigger: The user types a goal on the Goals page, or asks Muse to move a goal forward from chat or the Goals page.

steps.action: Submits a goal or a nudge, which is sent as a normal chat message
steps.label: Ask for a goal

steps.action: Plans the goal with 3 to 6 steps and an optional target and deadline
steps.label: Plan the goal

steps.action: Saves the goal through the goals handler
steps.label: Save the goal

steps.action: For a résumé step the user wants moved forward, checks the Library first and marks the step done only if a document matches
steps.label: Library check

steps.action: Runs a real tool for the step, then asks to mark it, naming the tool as evidence
steps.label: Ask to mark the step

steps.action: Refuses doing or done unless a non-bookkeeping tool ran this turn and matches the evidence
steps.label: Checks the evidence

steps.action: Saves the accepted status; the user can also click a step on the Goals page
steps.label: Save the status

steps.action: Records job applications; applied needs an approved Submit click or a confirmation email this turn
steps.label: Track applications

errorPaths: The goals API returns 400 for a missing goal, no steps, a bad status, an unknown step or an invalid application. It returns 404 for an unknown goal and 405 for unsupported methods.
update_step throws a refusal that tells the model to do the work with a tool first or cite the right tool.
track_application refuses a status the turn's actions do not prove, or moving a status backward. The model is told to ask the user to click the status on the Goals page.
If the Library has no résumé, the shortcut replies that it could not verify the step and asks the user to add one or click the step.
If the user declines or does not answer an approval for interview or offer, nothing is saved.

workflows.name: How Google connectors sign in
workflows.summary: Gmail and Calendar share one Google sign-in. The server keeps the tokens in an HttpOnly cookie, and the browser only learns whether Google is connected.
workflows.trigger: The user clicks Connect on the Gmail or Calendar card.

steps.action: Clicks Connect and reads the consent panel listing what Muse can do.
Continue with Google navigates the browser to the authorize endpoint.
The Google route adapter calls the authorize handler, which redirects to Google.
Google asks for consent and redirects back.
The callback handler exchanges the code and sets the tokens in a cookie.
At boot and after the redirect, initConnectors asks whether Google is connected and turns Gmail and Calendar on or off together.
When connected, the mail and calendar tools join the agent’s tools on the server and call Google with the tokens from the cookie; writes go through approval
On Disconnect Google, calls the endpoint, turns both connectors off and records an audit entry.

errorPaths: If the status call fails, both Google connectors are set off.
The Google route adapter turns a thrown error into a JSON error with its status, or 500, and keeps any cookie the error carries. Unknown actions return 404.
The disconnect call's failure is ignored, and the connectors are still turned off locally.

workflows.name: How documents enter the Library
workflows.summary: A user pastes text or uploads a file. The server stores only the extracted text, and the agent can then search and cite it.
workflows.trigger: The user submits the Library form, or Muse calls docs_add.

steps.action: Pastes text with a title or chooses a file such as a PDF, DOCX or TXT.
Sends the text or the base64 file. The docs_add tool does the same for text Muse saves.
Pasted text needs a title and text and is cut to 60,000 characters. Files are decoded and checked for empty or over 3MB.
Extracts text from an uploaded file. The filename without its extension is the default title.
Stores the document text for the user in Postgres. The original file is not kept. Returns 201 with the doc.
steps.label: Stores the text

steps.action: Adds the document to the list on the page; the docs_search and docs_read tools on the server read it from Postgres
steps.label: Adds it to the list

errorPaths: A missing title or text returns 400. An empty or undecodable file returns 400.
A file over 3MB returns 413.
A file with no extractable text returns 422.
Delete returns 404 for an unknown document. Unsupported methods return 405.

workflows.name: How the daily check-in runs
workflows.summary: Once a day, or when the user clicks the button, the open app starts a turn in which Muse works on the user’s goals without being asked and leaves a short progress brief. The turn runs on the server, but only an open app can start it.
workflows.trigger: The app is open after 9am with Every day on and no check-in yet today, or the user clicks the check-in button

steps.action: Checks every five minutes, and 20 seconds after the app opens, whether a check-in is due: Every day is on, none ran today, it is after 9am, Muse is free and there is a goal
steps.label: Is a check-in due?

steps.action: Records today as the last check-in and starts a check-in turn on the server
steps.label: Start the check-in turn

steps.action: Uses the fixed check-in instruction: the user is away, do what can be done alone, do not send emails, never submit an application
steps.label: Use the check-in instruction

steps.action: Searches Gmail for application confirmations and employer replies
steps.label: Check Gmail

steps.action: Updates tracked applications and works out pace against the target and deadline
steps.label: Update applications

steps.action: When behind pace, searches the watched companies’ hiring pages and scores new postings against the résumé
steps.label: Find and score postings

steps.action: Saves the three-line progress brief and what needs the user’s decision; it shows in chat on every device
steps.label: Leave the brief

errorPaths: If the app is closed, nothing starts: there is no server-side scheduler. Once started, the turn finishes even if the tab closes.
If Muse is busy, the assistant is unavailable or there are no goals, the check-in is skipped and tried again five minutes later.
"Do not send emails" is an instruction to the model, not a tool restriction: mail_send is still offered, and its approval card is what stops an email being sent while the user is away.

workflows.name: How Muse fills an application in Chrome
workflows.summary: Muse fills in a job application in the user’s own Chrome tab: the agent runtime on the server asks the Mini Muse tab that started the turn to run each browser tool through the extension, and only submits after the user approves.
workflows.trigger: The user asks Muse to fill in a specific application they chose

steps.action: Asks to open the application, read its fields and fill them from the Library résumé
steps.label: Ask for browser tools

steps.action: Creates a wait record and sends the tool to the tab that started the turn
steps.label: Relay to the tab

steps.action: Passes the request to the extension by window message, checking the reply comes from the same origin
steps.label: Hand to the extension

steps.action: Accepts only messages from the Mini Muse origins, picks the last non–Mini Muse tab, checks site permission and injects the form script
steps.label: Target the tab

steps.action: Reads or fills the fields in the tab, skipping passwords, SSNs and card or account numbers
steps.label: Fill, skip sensitive

steps.action: Posts the tool’s result back so the waiting turn continues
steps.label: Return the result

steps.action: Reviews the filled form in Chrome and approves the Submit click on the approval card
steps.label: Review and approve

steps.action: Relays the Submit click to the tab the same way
steps.label: Submit

errorPaths: If the tab that started the turn doesn’t answer within 45 seconds (it may be closed), the tool fails and Muse is told not to retry browser tools this turn.
Without the extension, the page’s request times out after 12 seconds with a message to use web_open or install it.
If the user hasn’t allowed control of the site, the extension refuses and asks them to allow it in its popup.
If the user doesn’t approve the click, nothing is clicked and the refusal goes back to Muse.

workflows.name: How turns are traced
workflows.summary: Each chat turn is recorded as a trace on the server, with the model calls and each tool as spans, so the builder can replay it on the Observability page. The browser still sends its own spans for page activity.
workflows.trigger: Any chat turn, model call or API request while tracing is on

steps.action: Loads the tracing settings at startup and starts spans for page activity
steps.label: Load tracing settings

steps.action: Sends a traceparent header with the turn request so the server’s spans join the page’s trace
steps.label: Link the turn

steps.action: Opens a span for the whole turn
steps.label: Trace the turn

steps.action: Records a span for each model call and tool, keeping text up to the cap or only its length
steps.label: Record spans

steps.action: Sends buffered page spans and logs every three seconds, and when the page is hidden or closed
steps.label: Ship page spans

steps.action: Stamps the signed-in user on traces and logs and writes the batch to Postgres
steps.label: Store the batch

steps.action: Opens the Observability page and a trace, which loads its spans for the waterfall
steps.label: Replay a trace

errorPaths: Every write is best-effort: a failed config load or flush never breaks the user’s request.
With OBS_ENABLED off, ingest accepts the batch and writes nothing.
Reading one trace by id doesn’t check who owns it, so anyone with a trace id can read its prompts and tool outputs.

limitations: The check-in steps that search Gmail and update applications follow the check-in instruction; which tools the model calls depends on the model.
I did not read the extension popup that grants site access.
